The company was formed in 2015 through a merger involving gloStream, a Troy, Michigan-based EHR vendor founded around 2005 that developed the gloEMR product. TRIARQ combined gloStream's EHR technology with practice management consulting and revenue cycle management services. In August 2021, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan acquired TRIARQ Health, and the company now operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of BCBSM. As of late 2021, TRIARQ had approximately 64 employees.\n\nTRIARQ's primary focus is on independent specialty practices, particularly in orthopedics, urology, and oncology, though they also serve cardiology, neurology, neurosurgery, pediatrics, and gastroenterology practices. Their business model is an MSO: they sell comprehensive practice management services (staffing, billing, compliance, supply chain, even real estate management) bundled with their proprietary EHR/PM technology platform called QSuite. They describe their mission as \"protecting the practice of independent medicine.\" The company is relatively small and niche, serving independent specialty practices rather than large health systems or hospitals.\n\n## Product: QSuite\n\nCHPL IDs: 10709\n\n### What It Is\n\nQSuite is TRIARQ's proprietary cloud-based integrated EHR and practice management platform. It evolved from gloStream's gloEMR product (which was originally built on Microsoft Office / Windows platform with CCHIT 2011 certification). QSuite is the technology backbone of TRIARQ's managed services offering. It is ONC-certified and Surescripts-certified. The product is hosted on Google Cloud Platform.\n\nQSuite is not just an EHR — it is an integrated platform spanning clinical documentation, practice management, billing/RCM, patient engagement, and analytics. TRIARQ markets it as part of their broader MSO offering, but the technology itself is the certified product. The product version certified on CHPL is \"Manistee\" (certified November 2021).\n\nThe certified module has broad certification: 40+ criteria spanning clinical data (a)(1)-(a)(15), transitions of care (b)(1)-(b)(3), clinical information reconciliation (b)(7)-(b)(9), patient portal/VDT (e)(1)-(e)(3), public health reporting (f)(1)-(f)(2), CQMs (c)(1)-(c)(4), FHIR APIs (g)(7)-(g)(10), and the EHI export requirement (b)(10). This is a comprehensive clinical EHR certification, not a narrow single-criterion product.\n\n### Users & Market\n\nTarget users (per CHPL SED description): \"doctors, nurses, physicians assistants, medical assistants, anyone entering or accessing clinical data at an ambulatory medical practice, anyone responsible for the training users and anyone responsible for system administration or IT of a medical practice.\"\n\nThe product serves independent ambulatory specialty practices. Specific specialties highlighted by the vendor include orthopedics, urology, oncology, cardiology, neurology, and gastroenterology. TRIARQ emphasizes that their technology is \"specialty-built\" — for example, marketing an \"orthopedic-built EHR\" on their orthopedics page.\n\nThe company is small (64 employees as of 2021). Customer count is not publicly disclosed on the website. Third-party review sites (SoftwareFinder, FindEMR) show very few reviews (1-2), suggesting a relatively small user base. One user review on SoftwareFinder rated it 4/5, saying \"it is a good EMR with potential to improve and be the best out there.\" A Capterra review mentioned being with the product for over 10 years and appreciating its customization and ease of use.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on vendor website, specialty pages, blog posts, and third-party review sites, QSuite includes the following modules and components:\n\n**EMR / Clinical Documentation**\n- Clinical charting and documentation\n- QScribe: AI-powered ambient listening that automatically generates structured clinical notes in the EHR (relatively new feature)\n- Customizable templates (inherited from gloEMR's template system)\n- Voice recognition functionality (a gloEMR legacy feature)\n\n**E-Prescribing**\n- Electronic prescribing (Surescripts-certified)\n- Integration with third-party EPCS (Electronic Prescribing of Controlled Substances) solutions\n\n**Practice Management (QPM)**\n- Appointment scheduling (including telehealth scheduling)\n- Patient registration and intake\n- Automated insurance and eligibility verification\n- Prior authorization management\n- Workflow automation\n- Real-time dashboards and KPI monitoring\n\n**QIntake**\n- Streamlined patient intake and registration portal\n- Patient-facing interface for onboarding\n\n**Patient Portal (MyQOne)**\n- Patient engagement between appointments\n- Access to medical results and bills\n- Treatment updates\n- Scheduling and billing access for patients\n\n**Billing / Revenue Cycle Management**\n- Built-in billing, coding, and tracking\n- Claims management (submission, corrections, resubmissions, appeals)\n- A/R management (automatic flagging of denied, underpaid, or unpaid claims)\n- Denial management\n- Patient payment tools and collections\n- QComplete: full-service RCM bundle combining QSuite technology with outsourced RCM team support\n\n**QInsights (Reporting & Analytics)**\n- Practice-specific financial dashboards\n- Revenue gap identification\n- Customizable cloud-based reporting\n- Monthly scorecards\n- Performance metrics and KPI tracking\n\n**QPathways (Care Management & Referral Networks)**\n- Referral network integration across providers, payers, and patients\n- Care coordination tools\n- Clinical and financial transparency platform\n- Value-based care support\n\n**Lab Integration**\n- Lab orders and results integration\n- Automatic updating of health records with new lab results\n- TRIARQ Connectors for secure links between office, patients, providers, off-site labs, and other facilities\n\n**Interoperability / Data Exchange**\n- Transitions of care / C-CDA support (certified for (b)(1)-(b)(3))\n- Direct messaging\n- FHIR API access (certified for (g)(7)-(g)(10))\n- Patient reminders\n- Public health reporting (immunization, syndromic surveillance)\n- MIPS quality measure reporting and attesting support\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the features and modules described above, QSuite stores and manages:\n\n- **Clinical data**: Patient demographics, medical histories, clinical notes (including AI-generated notes via QScribe), problems, medications, allergies, vital signs, lab orders and results, immunizations, procedures, clinical decision support data\n- **Prescriptions**: E-prescribing data including controlled substance prescriptions (via EPCS integration), medication histories, Surescripts data\n- **Scheduling data**: Appointments, telehealth scheduling, patient location tracking from admission to discharge\n- **Patient intake/registration**: Contact information, insurance information, eligibility verification data, intake forms\n- **Billing and financial data**: Claims, charge capture, coding data, A/R records, denial records, payment data, insurance eligibility responses, prior authorizations\n- **Patient portal data**: Patient messages, portal access logs, shared documents and results\n- **Lab data**: Lab orders, lab results (integrated from external labs)\n- **Referral data**: Referral network information, care coordination records via QPathways\n- **Quality/reporting data**: CQM/MIPS quality measure data, public health reporting submissions\n- **Administrative data**: User accounts, staff tasks, practice configuration\n- **Analytics/reporting data**: Dashboards, KPI snapshots, financial reports, scorecards\n\nThe vendor website does not specifically mention document management/scanning, imaging/PACS integration, or faxing capabilities, though these could exist without being prominently marketed. The blog post about comprehensive practice management mentions that TRIARQ handles \"everything except patient examination and diagnosis,\" suggesting the platform touches nearly all practice operations. This is notably more effort than most vendors put into (b)(10) documentation.\n\n### Export Format\n\nThe EHI Export produces a multi-format package:\n\n1. **CCDA XML files** — HL7 C-CDA documents compliant with USCDI v3, using C-CDA R2.1 Companion Guide Release 4.1. These contain the standard clinical summary data (problems, medications, allergies, labs, vitals, immunizations, etc.).\n\n2. **CSV files** — 27 structured data categories exported as CSV, each with a defined schema. This is the bulk of the export and covers data domains beyond what CCDA/USCDI includes. Categories span clinical, billing, administrative, and document management data.\n\n3. **PDF files** — 8 document types exported as PDF: Patient Messages, Lab Orders Documents, Exam Notes, Patient Letters, Patient Consent, Patient Order Templates, Nurse Notes, Patient Education.\n\n4. **Word files** — 6 document types exported as Word: Exam Notes, Nurse Notes, Billing Statements, Collections, Triage Templates, Patient Forms.\n\n5. **Image files** — 4 image types: Driver License, Insurance Card, DMS Documents, Other.\n\nThe documentation states: \"The EHI Export feature also supports generating single-patient ePHI exports as well as bulk data exports for larger patient populations. This functionality is available in QSuite Manistee v12.12 and later.\"\n\n### Data Dictionary Detail\n\nThe CSV data dictionary provides field-level documentation for 777 fields across 30 modules (plus 2 parent-only categories). Each field has:\n- **Name**: Column name (e.g., `PatientID`, `VisitDate`, `NDCCode`)\n- **Description**: Human-readable description (e.g., \"Patient Identifier\", \"Visit Date\", \"NDC Code\")\n- **Type**: Data type — `numeric`, `text`, or `date`\n\nThe largest entity is **Demographic** with 105 fields, covering extensive patient demographics including name, address, SSN, race, ethnicity, language, emergency contacts, employer information, and more. **Medication** has 52 fields, **Immunization** has 51, **Vitals** has 48, and **OB Vitals** has 43.\n\nThe **Patient Cases** resource type is actually a parent grouping for 4 sub-entities: Patient Cases - Master (24 fields), Patient Cases - Diagnosis (6 fields), Patient Cases - Insurance Plan (6 fields), and Patient Cases - Prior Authorization Master (20 fields). Similarly, **Prior Authorization** (16 fields) has a related **Prior Authorization Master** (20 fields) entity.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\n**Clearly covered clinical domains:**\n- Demographics (105 fields — very comprehensive)\n- Allergies (25 fields, including SNOMED codes and NDC codes)\n- Problems/Diagnoses (21 fields)\n- Medications (52 fields, (Word export)\n\n**Clearly covered document/image domains:**\n- DMS Document Index (CSV listing of all documents)\n- DMS Documents (image export)\n- Driver License images\n- Insurance Card images\n- Patient Order Templates (PDF export)\n\n**Audit trail:**\n- Audit Trail (11 fields) — included in the export, though audit logs are not strictly EHI\n\n**Potentially missing or unclear domains:**\n- **E-prescribing details**: While Medication has 52 fields, there's no separate e-prescribing or prescription history entity capturing EPCS transactions, pharmacy responses, or Surescripts data\n- **Lab results (structured)**: Lab Orders Documents are exported as PDFs, but there's no CSV entity for structured lab result values. If lab results are captured as structured data in QSuite (which is likely given their lab integration features), exporting only PDFs loses queryability\n- **Clinical notes content**: Exam Notes and Nurse Notes are exported as PDF and Word documents, but there's no structured CSV entity for note metadata or content — this is reasonable for free-text notes but means note metadata (author, date, note type, status) may not be separately queryable\n- **QScribe AI-generated notes**: No specific mention of how AI-generated clinical notes are handled in the export\n- **QPathways referral network data**: The Referrals CSV has 33 fields, but the broader QPathways care coordination data (if stored) is not specifically mentioned\n- **QInsights analytics/reporting data**: No mention of exported dashboards or custom reports — though this is analytics data, not necessarily EHI\n- **Patient portal access/activity data**: No entity for portal interaction data beyond Patient-Provider Messages\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe multi-format approach is thoughtful and well-suited to the data:\n\n- **CCDA for clinical summaries**: Appropriate use of the standard for the USCDI clinical data slice\n- **CSV for structured tabular data**: Good choice for the broader data — billing, scheduling, administrative data that doesn't map well to FHIR or CCDA. CSV is widely accessible and importable.\n- **PDF/Word for documents**: Appropriate for clinical notes, letters, forms, and other document-centric content\n- **Images for scanned documents**: Driver licenses, insurance cards, DMS documents as image files\n\nThis is a genuine (b)(10) implementation, not a (g)(10) FHIR API relabeled. The export goes well beyond USCDI to include billing (charges, denials, refunds, reserves), insurance, prior authorization, patient cases, appointments, pharmacy, and document management data. The use of CSV for structured data and PDF/Word for documents shows the vendor understands the distinction between structured and unstructured health information.\n\nThe data types in the dictionary are limited to `numeric`, `text`, and `date` — no distinction between integer/decimal, no string length constraints, and no explicit foreign key documentation. Relationships between entities must be inferred from field naming conventions (e.g., `PatientID` appears across most entities).\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Strengths:**\n- Purpose-built web application for the documentation — not a buried PDF or afterthought\n- Field-level data dictionary with 777 fields across 30+ entities\n- Clear descriptions for each entity and field\n- Data types specified for every field\n- Searchable interface with sidebar navigation\n- Comprehensive coverage of both CSV entities and non-CSV export file types\n\n**Weaknesses:**\n- Data types are coarse (`numeric`, `text`, `date`) — no precision on numeric types, no string length limits, no datetime format specification\n- No value set documentation — coded fields (e.g., `HistoryStatus`, `HistoryCategory`, `Reaction`) don't list valid values\n- No relationship/foreign key documentation — you must infer joins from matching field names like `PatientID` and `VisitID`\n- No sample data or example export files\n- No export instructions or user guide for performing the export\n- CCDA export documented only by reference to HL7 standards — no vendor-specific customizations or constraints documented\n- No documentation of file naming conventions, directory structure, or packaging of the export\n- No documentation of how documents are associated with patients in the DMS export (only an index CSV plus image files)\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\nThe data dictionary is well-structured with consistent field definitions across all entities. Each field has a name, description, and type. The granularity is at the field level (column names and types), which is the right level for a CSV export format. However, the documentation stops short of being truly implementation-ready due to the lack of:\n\n1. Value set documentation for coded fields\n2. Foreign key/relationship documentation\n3. Export packaging documentation (directory structure, file naming)\n4. Sample data\n\nA developer attempting to import this data could build a reasonable schema from the field definitions, but would need to reverse-engineer relationships and valid values from actual export data.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL: https://ehi.myqone.com/\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: yes (Angular SPA, content rendered via JavaScript)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link (main page has everything; CSV detail pages are one click deep)\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\n- The site is an Angular SPA, so `curl` of the HTML returns only the shell.
